Motion Studio / follow-up / 2026-11-11

A more convincing stride.
A faster start, by choice.

Articulated running, ground-matched foot contact and a restrained sense of speed. Standard stays at 10 m/s; Fast is a deliberate switch to a 14 m/s opening. The game remains single player, with the same fair pause and identity rules.

FAST START DEFAULTS OFFORIGINAL 3D CHARACTERSCAMERA-FREE EVIDENCE

Issue #39 · PR #44 · Original implementation and reference-footage report

What changed and why

The first runner moved straight limbs as rigid pendulums. This follow-up gives the character separate hips, knees, ankles, shoulders and elbows, with a planted stance, toe-off and folded recovery. The faster opening is optional so the existing Standard pace stays available for learning and later physical trials.

Both screenshots come from the actual local-server application. The before image is historical. New captures use synthetic controls; no participant footage or private camera image is included.

Fast is an explicit setup choice

Standard · default

Fast start off. Begin at 10 m/s and increase by 0.035 m/s each active second, capped at 18 m/s.

Fast · opt in

Fast start on. Begin at 14 m/s with the same gradual increase and 18 m/s cap. Obstacle rules, skins and player admission remain the same.

  • The switch is locked during countdown, play and pause. Change it before starting a new run.
  • New run retains the chosen pace on the current page. A fresh page or reload resets Fast to off; the choice is not persisted.
  • The HUD identifies Fast during play. Rehearsal remains usable without Python, camera capture or inference.

Small speed-responsive camera framing and lane follow add energy without camera shake or visual effects covering hazards. System reduced-motion preferences remove optional camera follow/FOV changes, decorative coin spin/bursts and hit flicker while preserving the essential game actions.

Inspect the full running cycle

A single still cannot show gait quality. The following contact sheet shows eight phase panels from the real Three.js renderer at 14 m/s, spanning 0/8 through 7/8 of a full cycle. Nine source poses were recorded, including the repeated 8/8 boundary retained in the embedded JSON. Each visible pose is derived from the paused game clock and distance; changing the phase to paused cannot snap the runner to idle.

Open the animated stride inspection · contains motion

The source cycle is 423.7 ms at 14 m/s (cadence 2.36 full cycles/s). The illustrated GIF repeats eight phase samples in approximately 420 ms. It is a synthetic pose sequence, not a recording of display FPS, sensor latency or a participant’s running cadence.

  1. Contact and toe-off: each stance travels 0.76 m relative to the advancing avatar. Its contact duration follows the current speed, matching the visible scrolling track instead of skating over it. Finite shoe corners stay above the ground.
  2. Recovery and opposing arms: two-bone leg geometry folds the knee and swings the foot through; separate elbow joints keep the arms bent and alternating. The belt and shoulders counter-rotate while the spine leans forward.
  3. Continuous timing: cycle = 1.8 × active seconds + 0.04 × traveled meters. The cadence changes continuously with speed; it is not recalculated by dividing distance by a changing stride length.
  4. Fair pause: pose, scenery and camera functions use game state. There is no wall-clock animation or per-render settling that could keep moving while tracking is paused. Jump and the compact tucked roll remain separate actions.

This is a stylized procedural animation with qualitative running cues, not a biomechanical model. Foot-plant tests include constant speeds of 10 / 14 / 18 m/s, the bounded acceleration ramp, actual transformed foot positions, cycle-boundary rounding, first-frame pause equality and three skin envelopes. The final check record below states which tests actually ran.

The setup choice survives a small screen

The in-stage Pause control and fixed lane / Jump / Roll dock keep the main actions available during phone-size play. Setup fields reflow without changing the one-player rule. New run returns to clear setup guidance; it must not retain an old paused warning.

Both opening paces, checked in simulation

48 / 48declared oracle cases with zero hits and exact alternate-player freeze
2 opening pacesStandard and Fast tested in both worlds
30 / 60 / 120 Hzsynthetic control rates across four seeds

48 cases: 2 worlds × Standard/Fast start × 4 seeds × 30/60/120 Hz; approximately 60 active seconds each, followed by 2 seconds with another player. The oracle selects known open lanes. This demonstrates authored pattern solvability and pause invariants; it does not measure human reaction difficulty, motion accuracy or participant safety.

Concurrent desktop workloads and the in-app browser can affect results. CPU submission timing includes the immutable game-state copy evaluated inside the timed call.

Hosted status: Local verification complete. PR #44 must pass software-checks on its latest commit before merge; consult its current Checks tab. Latest-commit CI remains a separate merge gate; local checks do not certify physical input or hardware capacity.

Independent critical review

No known blocking software or visual defect remains in the reviewed follow-up after the foot-sliding and stale ready-message fixes. The requested pace choice and a materially more natural procedural sprint are implemented. The lead reports that final integrated local checks and the build passed; the change is ready for PR review, with latest-commit hosted CI required before merge. This is not a perfect-score claim, commercial-game parity or physical motion certification.

Reviewed dimensionScoreEvidence and limits
Opening pace choice and configuration fidelity9.0 / 10Fast start defaults off at 10 m/s; explicit opt-in starts at 14 m/s. Both opening values and the 18 m/s cap are visible before selection. The boolean is validated, snapshotted and locked during countdown/play/pause; a new run retains the choice without changing the seeded obstacle layout.
Procedural sprint articulation and readability8.5 / 10The timestamped stride sheet shows alternating contact, push-off, flight and folded recovery with opposing bent arms. Articulated hip/knee/ankle and shoulder/elbow chains, mild lean and belt/shoulder counterturn are materially better than the previous rigid pendulums. The art remains stylized low-poly animation rather than motion-captured or biomechanically calibrated movement.
Ground contact and visual geometry9.0 / 10The corrected stance path follows the scrolling track. Reviewed tests check pure and actual transformed ankle velocity at 10/14/18 m/s, the acceleration ramp, finite shoe vertices, rig reach and all three skins. Decorative pelvis yaw is separated from the leg targets to avoid reintroducing skating.
Determinism, pause and existing safety preservation9.0 / 10Pose and camera derive from game time, distance and state rather than render-history integration. Tests compare different renderer histories and the first playing-to-paused frame. The lead additionally reports exact canvas-pixel equality for an unchanged playing/paused inspection pose. Lane/collision/identity policy is unchanged; both pace profiles retain simulation pause invariants in the declared oracle workload.
Desktop and mobile GUI clarity9.0 / 10Fresh screenshots show the default off switch, locked Fast selection during an active run, visible Fast speed feedback, in-stage Pause and the mobile touch dock. A confirmed stale pause instruction after New run was fixed and the corrected ready-state screenshot was inspected. A full assistive-technology compliance audit was not performed.
Reference gameplay pattern readability9.0 / 10Compared with the selected documented reference frames, the updated game retains clear three-lane depth, visible coin routes, distinguishable train/hurdle/overhead hazards and an uncluttered rear chase silhouette. The stride sequence adds temporal articulation evidence that a single gameplay screenshot could not provide.
Commercial reference polish and breadth6.5 / 10Subway Surfers and Talking Tom Gold Run still show substantially richer scenery, materials, character-animation variety, audiovisual feedback and gameplay-content breadth. The new animation and selectable pace do not establish commercial parity or a measured match to their speed or cadence.

This follow-up makes no perfect-score or commercial-parity claim. The original commercial-game reference frames and their bounded comparison remain in the original implementation report; no new reference-game frame timing or reaction-time measurement was performed here.

Physical work is still ahead

Camera capture stayed off for this follow-up. Physical trials are planned for 2026-11-12, tomorrow relative to this report’s 2026-11-11 work date, and have not been performed here. Comfortable lane reach, jump/duck recognition across heights, spectator occlusion, actual identity stability and externally observed action-to-display latency remain unverified.

The game continues to use one anonymous joined slot. Another detected person freezes movement, hazards, time and score; identity or camera-space changes require a fresh run. Skins remain cosmetic and do not change scoring or collision behavior.

English is the supported language. All new game evidence uses synthetic rehearsal or deterministic renderer inspection, with no participant data, credentials or camera footage.
